biological.citation: Identification of Variant-Specific Functions of PIK3CA by Rapid Phenotyping of Rare Mutations (PMID: 26627007)
biological.summary: High-throughput functional assessment of PIK3CA tail mutations using in vitro and in vivo cell growth and transformation assays differentiated driver from passenger mutations. PIK3CA variants above 5% mutation frequency were significantly more oncogenic than wild-type in all assays, while variants at 0.07–5.0% showed variable oncogenic activity. Proteomic profiling revealed variant-specific activation of PI3K signaling and the MEK1/2 module of the MAPK pathway.

biological.citation: Organismal metabolism regulates the expansion of oncogenic PIK3CA mutant clones in normal esophagus (PMID: 39169259)
biological.summary: Expression of heterozygous Pik3ca H1047R in transgenic mice drives clonal expansion in normal esophageal epithelium by tilting cell fate toward proliferation via the PI3K-mTOR pathway. Metabolic conditions such as type 1 diabetes or diet-induced obesity enhanced the competitive fitness of Pik3ca H1047R cells, while metformin reduced mutant cell advantage in vivo and in vitro. Higher density of PIK3CA gain-of-function mutations was found in the esophagus of individuals with high BMI compared to normal weight.

biological.citation: Oncogenic PIK3CA corrupts growth factor signaling specificity (PMID: 39706867)
biological.summary: Using live-cell imaging of PI3K/AKT activity reporters and CyTOF measurements, dose-dependent expression of PIK3CA H1047R in human cervical cancer and iPSCs was found to corrupt the fidelity of growth factor-induced information transfer rather than acting as a simple constitutive activator. PIK3CA H1047R preferentially amplified EGFR signaling responses compared to IGF1 and insulin receptor signaling, and also enhanced signaling heterogeneity. This demonstrates that oncogenic PIK3CA H1047R corrupts information transfer in a growth factor-dependent manner.

biological.citation: Oncogenic PIK3CA recruits myeloid-derived suppressor cells to shape the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment in luminal breast cancer through the 5-lipoxygenase-dependent arachidonic acid pathway (PMID: 37965796)
biological.summary: PIK3CA mutant luminal breast cancer cells induce an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by recruiting myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) and excluding cytotoxic T cells via the arachidonic acid metabolism pathway. Mechanistically, PIK3CA mutations activate transcription of 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) in a STAT3-dependent manner, leading to high LTB4 production that binds BLT2 on MDSCs and promotes their infiltration. Targeted therapy against the PI3K/5-LOX/LTB4 axis combined with immune checkpoint blockade achieved dramatic tumor shrinkage in vivo.

biological.citation: PIK3CA Mutations Downregulate PPT1 to Promote Adipogenesis by Suppressing P300 Depalmitoylation and Phase Separation (PMID: 41610323)
biological.summary: PIK3CA mutations transcriptionally repress PPT1 via PI3K-AKT-c-JUN signaling in facial infiltrating lipomatosis (FIL), leading to enhanced palmitoylation of the transcriptional coactivator P300 at C1176. This palmitoylation stabilizes P300 by impairing its chaperone-mediated lysosomal degradation and inhibits P300 phase separation, thereby preserving its histone acetyltransferase activity and promoting chromatin accessibility and expression of adipogenic genes. This establishes a novel 'palmitoylation-phase separation-epigenetic regulation' axis linking PIK3CA mutation to excessive adipogenesis.

biological.citation: BEX2 regulates autophagy by inhibiting PIK3CA-p85 interaction in non-small-cell lung cancer cells (PMID: 41398291)
biological.summary: BEX2 was found to physically interact with PIK3CA (the PI3K catalytic subunit) in NSCLC cell lines (A549, H1792, H1299) and impairs the interaction between PIK3CA and p85 (the PI3K regulatory subunit), thereby inhibiting PI3K activity. This BEX2-PIK3CA interaction promotes autophagic flux through suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling. The regulatory role of BEX2 on autophagy was confirmed to be dependent on the presence of PIK3CA.

biological.citation: miR-29a Downregulates PIK3CA Expression and Inhibits Cervical Cancer Cell Dynamics: A Comparative Clinical Analysis (PMID: 39590348)
biological.summary: miR-29a was shown to bind the 3'-UTR region of PIK3CA, leading to reduction in PIK3CA expression at both RNA and protein levels in PIK3CA-overexpressing cervical cancer cell lines (SiHa, C33A, HeLa). Transfection of miR-29a into HeLa cells reduced cell division and migration as demonstrated by wound healing and cell migration assays. Clinical biopsy samples from cervical cancer patients showed correlation between miR-29a concentration and disease progression.

biological.citation: Neddylation as a target in PIK3CA-mutated head and neck cancer (PMID: 40154000)
biological.summary: CRISPRi-based genome-wide screening in an HPV-positive HNSCC cell line (UM-SCC-47) engineered to express the canonical E545K PIK3CA mutant identified 34 genes co-dependent on PIK3CA E545K mutation, including 5 genes in the neddylation pathway (NEDD8, NEDD8-MDP-1, NAE1, USP8, UBA3). Validation experiments confirmed the essential role of NEDD8, NEDD8-MDP-1, and NAE1, indicating a novel regulatory mechanism in PIK3CA E545K-mutated HNSCC. These findings suggest PIK3CA mutation may serve as a predictive biomarker for neddylation inhibitor therapy.

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Dual inhibition of mTORC1 and mTORC2 activation effectively rescues hyperproliferative lymphatic sprouting in a cell-based model system of complex lymphatic anomalies (M. Battig et al.)
biological.summary: Expression of PIK3CA H1047L in human dermal lymphatic endothelial cells resulted in significantly greater lymphangiogenic sprouting compared to wild-type controls (cumulative sprout length 2666 µm vs. 1381 µm, p=0.029), with immunoblotting revealing over-activation of mTORC1 and mTORC2 targets. Dual mTORC1/mTORC2 inhibition with OSI-027 rescued the hyperproliferative phenotype caused by PIK3CA H1047L to basal levels. These findings demonstrate that somatic activating PIK3CA mutations drive lymphangiogenesis through over-activation of AKT/mTOR signaling.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - Multi-ancestry genome-wide meta-analysis in Parkinson's disease (J. Kim et al.)
biological.summary: A large-scale multi-ancestry meta-analysis of Parkinson's disease GWASes incorporating data from 49,049 PD cases, 18,785 proxy cases, and 2,458,063 controls identified PIK3CA as one of 12 potential novel genome-wide significant risk loci for Parkinson's disease. PIK3CA was nominated as a putative risk gene near one of the novel loci using summary-based Mendelian randomization with multi-omic data. This represents a genetic association of PIK3CA with Parkinson's disease risk across ancestrally diverse populations.
